  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Charles de Bourcy<sup id="id1.1" class="ltx_sup">*</sup>, Sahra Ghalebikesabi<sup id="id1.2" class="ltx_sup">*</sup>, Avi Schwarzschild<sup id="id1.3" class="ltx_sup">*</sup>, Alex Gorbachev<sup id="id1.4" class="ltx_sup">*</sup>, Mihai Maruseac<sup id="id1.5" class="ltx_sup">*</sup></span>
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><span id="id2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Annie Chu, Vol Kyrylov, Tong Mu, Ally Bennett, Andy Nguyen, Casey Meehan, Jessica Gan Lee</span>
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><span id="id3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Shane Bauer, Harold Nguyen, Rodolpho Eckhardt, Yuqi Liu, Charlie Oxborough, Marco Rougeth</span>
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><span id="id4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Omar Chedid, Caio Costa, Yash Parikh, Yao Li, Congzheng Song, Om Thakkar, Vinnie Monaco</span>
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><sup id="id5" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">*</span></sup><span id="id6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Co-lead authors</span>
</span></span></span></span></div>
<div class="ltx_dates">August 24, 2026</div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">OpenAI Privacy Filter is a compact, bidirectional token-classification model for detecting and redacting personally identifiable information (PII) and secrets in unstructured text.
The model is derived from an autoregressively pretrained checkpoint and converted into a bidirectional, banded-attention classifier that labels an input sequence in a single forward pass.
A constrained Viterbi decoder produces coherent spans across eight privacy categories and exposes configurable operating points for precision–recall tradeoffs.
Privacy Filter has 1.5 billion total parameters, 50 million active parameters per token, and a 128,000-token context window.
It is designed for efficient local deployment and domain-specific fine-tuning.
Privacy Filter is intended as a configurable data-minimization component within layered privacy workflows, not as an anonymization or compliance guarantee.</p>
  
</div>

<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OpenAI Privacy Filter is a bidirectional token-classification model for personally identifiable information (PII) detection and redaction in text. It is designed for high-throughput privacy workflows, and is able to perform context-aware detection of PII in unstructured text.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S1.F1.pic1" class="ltx_picture ltx_centering" height="122.84" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 637 122.84" width="637"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,122.84) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#E8E8E8;" fill="#E8E8E8" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 8.3 L 0 114.54 C 0 119.13 3.72 122.84 8.3 122.84 L 628.7 122.84 C 633.28 122.84 637 119.13 637 114.54 L 637 8.3 C 637 3.72 633.28 0 628.7 0 L 8.3 0 C 3.72 0 0 3.72 0 8.3 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 8.3 L 1.38 114.54 C 1.38 118.36 4.48 121.46 8.3 121.46 L 628.7 121.46 C 632.52 121.46 635.61 118.36 635.61 114.54 L 635.61 8.3 C 635.61 4.48 632.52 1.38 628.7 1.38 L 8.3 1.38 C 4.48 1.38 1.38 4.48 1.38 8.3 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 16.39 46.89)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:43.67em;--ltx-fo-height:4.5em;--ltx-fo-depth:2.4em;font-size:10pt;" height="95.6" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 62.33)" width="604.27"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S1.F1.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:43.67em;">

<span id="S1.F1.pic1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<span id="S1.F1.pic1.p4.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S1.F1.pic1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;--ltx-fg-color:#6B7280;">Privacy Filter</span></span>
</span>
<span id="S1.F1.pic1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S1.F1.pic1.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" color="#000000" height="30" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 495.46 30" width="495.46"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,30) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#A7F3D0;" fill="#A7F3D0" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 10.24 L 0 19.76 C 0 25.42 4.58 30 10.24 30 L 485.22 30 C 490.88 30 495.46 25.42 495.46 19.76 L 495.46 10.24 C 495.46 4.58 490.88 0 485.22 0 L 10.24 0 C 4.58 0 0 4.58 0 10.24 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#ECFDF5;" fill="#ECFDF5" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.55 10.24 L 0.55 19.76 C 0.55 25.11 4.89 29.45 10.24 29.45 L 485.22 29.45 C 490.57 29.45 494.91 25.11 494.91 19.76 L 494.91 10.24 C 494.91 4.89 490.57 0.55 485.22 0.55 L 10.24 0.55 C 4.89 0.55 0.55 4.89 0.55 10.24 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 11.41 4.49)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:34.16em;--ltx-fo-height:1.32em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="18.25" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 18.25)" width="472.68"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

<span id="S1.F1.pic1.p2.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.F1.pic1.p2.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#1F2937;">lives at
<span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S1.F1.pic1.p2.pic1.pic2" class="ltx_picture" height="18.25" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-6.7px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 73.78 18.25" width="73.78"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#1F2937;--ltx-fill-color:#1F2937;" fill="#1F2937" stroke="#1F2937" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,18.25) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FDA4AF;" fill="#FDA4AF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0.83 L 0 17.42 C 0 17.88 0.37 18.25 0.83 18.25 L 72.95 18.25 C 73.41 18.25 73.78 17.88 73.78 17.42 L 73.78 0.83 C 73.78 0.37 73.41 0 72.95 0 L 0.83 0 C 0.37 0 0 0.37 0 0.83 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFF1F2;" fill="#FFF1F2" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.83 0.83 L 0.83 17.42 L 72.95 17.42 L 72.95 0.83 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 4.77 6.7)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:6.66em;--ltx-fo-height:0.7em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.2em;font-size:7pt;" height="8.72" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 6.78)" width="64.52"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S1.F1.pic1.p2.pic1.pic2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:78%;--ltx-fg-color:#BE123C;">private_address</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>. Call him at
<span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S1.F1.pic1.p2.pic1.pic3" class="ltx_picture" height="18.25" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-6.7px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 68.24 18.25" width="68.24"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#1F2937;--ltx-fill-color:#1F2937;" fill="#1F2937" stroke="#1F2937" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,18.25) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FDA4AF;" fill="#FDA4AF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0.83 L 0 17.42 C 0 17.88 0.37 18.25 0.83 18.25 L 67.41 18.25 C 67.87 18.25 68.24 17.88 68.24 17.42 L 68.24 0.83 C 68.24 0.37 67.87 0 67.41 0 L 0.83 0 C 0.37 0 0 0.37 0 0.83 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFF1F2;" fill="#FFF1F2" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.83 0.83 L 0.83 17.42 L 67.41 17.42 L 67.41 0.83 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 4.77 6.7)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:6.09em;--ltx-fo-height:0.7em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.2em;font-size:7pt;" height="8.72" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 6.78)" width="58.98"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S1.F1.pic1.p2.pic1.pic3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:78%;--ltx-fg-color:#BE123C;">private_phone</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</span></span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>Illustrative chat-style interaction showing Privacy Filter redacting PII from raw user text.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy Filter is pretrained autoregressively to arrive at a checkpoint with similar architecture to gpt-oss, albeit of a smaller size. We then converted that checkpoint into a bidirectional token classifier over a privacy label taxonomy and post-trained it with a supervised classification loss. For architecture details about gpt-oss, see the <a href="https://openai.com/index/gpt-oss-model-card/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">gpt-oss model card</a>. Instead of generating text token by token, Privacy Filter labels an input sequence in a single forward pass, then decodes coherent spans with a constrained Viterbi procedure. For each input token, the model predicts a probability distribution over the label taxonomy, which consists of the eight output categories detailed in <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Model Architecture ‣ 2 Model Details ‣ Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>. Privacy Filter provides the community with a free-to-download, easy-to-use, and tunable model with the following practical strengths:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Permissive license: We are releasing Privacy Filter under the Apache 2.0 license, allowing for experimentation, customization, and commercial deployment.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Small footprint: Privacy Filter is a small model that can run in a web browser or on a laptop; it contains 1.5 billion total parameters and 50 million active parameters.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Fine-tunable: While the out-of-the-box performance is strong, Privacy Filter can be further adapted to specific data distributions through simple and data-efficient fine-tuning.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Long-context: The 128,000 token context window enables processing long text with high throughput and no chunking.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Runtime control: Privacy Filter ships with span decoding that users can configure to control the precision-recall tradeoffs and detected span lengths.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy protection for AI systems is an ongoing effort across research, product design, evaluation, and deployment.
Privacy Filter reflects one direction we believe is important: small, efficient models with frontier capability in narrowly defined tasks that matter for real-world AI systems. We are releasing it because we think privacy-preserving infrastructure should be easier to inspect, run, adapt, and improve.
Our goal is for models to learn about the world, not about private individuals. Privacy Filter helps make that possible.
We’re releasing this preview of Privacy Filter to receive feedback from the research and privacy communities and iterate further on model performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Model Details</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy Filter is a bidirectional token classification model with span decoding. It is trained in phases, beginning with autoregressive pretraining. The pretrained language model is then modified and post-trained as a bidirectional banded attention token classifier with band size 128 (effective attention window: 257 tokens including self). At inference time, we apply constrained sequence decoding to produce coherent <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside%E2%80%93outside%E2%80%93beginning_(tagging)" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">BIOES</a> (Begin, Inside, Outside, End, Single) span labels.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Model Architecture</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As a bidirectional attention-based model, Privacy Filter has several standard components. Privacy Filter uses a pre-norm transformer encoder-style stack. The model begins with token embeddings and then passes those representations through eight repeated transformer blocks. Within each block, attention uses grouped-query attention with rotary positional embeddings, with 14 query heads and 2 key-value heads, corresponding to a group size of 7 query heads per key-value head. The feed-forward sublayers are implemented as sparse mixture-of-experts blocks with 128 experts total and top-4 routing per token. The final layer is a token-classification head over privacy labels, rather than a natural-language vocabulary, and uses a residual-stream width of <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{model}}=640" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>model</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>640</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{model}}=640</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Relative to iterative autoregressive approaches, this design allows all tokens to be labeled in one pass, which is important for throughput-sensitive applications. Relative to classical masked-language-model pretraining approaches, this is a post-training conversion of an autoregressive model rather than a native masked-LM setup.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Output Shape</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy Filter can detect 8 privacy span categories:</p>
<ol id="S2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">account_number</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_address</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_email</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_person</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_phone</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_url</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">7.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_date</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">8.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">secret</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To perform token-classification, each non-background span category is expanded into boundary-tagged token classes: <span id="S2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">B-&lt;label&gt;</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">I-&lt;label&gt;</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">E-&lt;label&gt;</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">S-&lt;label&gt;</span>, plus the background class, <span id="S2.SS2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">O</span>. So the total number of token-level output classes is 33: 1 background class + 8 span labels * 4 boundary tags = 33 classes. Thus, the output head emits 33 logits for each token. For a sequence of length <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, the output has shape <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[T,33]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>33</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[T,33]</annotation></semantics></math>; for a batch of size B, it has shape <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[B,T,33]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>33</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[B,T,33]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The token-label vocabulary consists of the background label <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">O</span> plus BIOES-tagged variants of each privacy category: <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">account_number</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_address</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_email</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_person</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_phone</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_url</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_date</span>, and <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">secret</span>. In other words, for each category, the model predicts <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">B-</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">I-</span>, <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">E-</span>, and <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">S-</span> forms corresponding to begin, inside, end, and single-token spans. At inference time, these per-token logits are decoded into coherent BIOES span labels using constrained sequence decoding.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>Sequence Decoding</h3>

<section id="S2.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.3.1 </span>Rationale</h4>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After the token classifier produces per-token logits, we decode labels with a constrained Viterbi decoder using linear-chain transition scoring, rather than taking an independent argmax for each token. The decoder enforces allowed BIOES boundary transitions and scores complete label paths with start, transition, and end terms, plus six transition-bias parameters that control background persistence, span entry, span continuation, span closure, and boundary-to-boundary handoff. This global path optimization is intended to improve span coherence and boundary stability by making each token decision depend on sequence-level structure, not just local logits, especially in noisy or mixed-format text where local token decisions alone can produce fragmented or inconsistent boundaries.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.3.2 </span>Operating-Point Calibration</h4>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sequence decoding parameters can discourage long spans of background classifications while encouraging redaction span starts and continuations, yielding broader and more contiguous redaction for improved recall. They can also be configured the other way for improved precision. At runtime, users can tune parameters that control this tradeoff.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Uses</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Intended Uses</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy Filter is intended for PII span detection in raw text and for passing detected spans to downstream redaction workflows. A useful way to think about the model is as a data minimization component: it identifies candidate sensitive spans and their classes, and the surrounding system decides whether to mask, remove, replace, pseudonymize, alert, or route them for review.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Representative applications include:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S3.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sanitizing text at ingestion time before storage, indexing, analytics, or retrieval.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Preparing corpora for model training, evaluation, logging, or internal sharing.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Redacting personal data and secrets in enterprise documents, email, support transcripts, and application logs.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Adapting the model to domain-specific privacy policies through fine-tuning and operating-point calibration.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Out-of-Scope and Misuse</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy Filter should not be treated as an anonymization, compliance, or safety guarantee, a substitute for policy review in high-stakes deployments, a universal privacy oracle with fixed behavior across all text genres and regions, or a legal determination system.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Potential misuse includes treating unredacted output as safe for release, relying on default operating points without validating them on the target distribution, or skipping domain adaptation when local policy requires materially stricter or materially broader redaction criteria.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Bias, Risks, and Limitations</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Over-reliance Risk</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy Filter is a redaction and data minimization aid, not an anonymization, compliance, or a safety guarantee. Over-reliance on the tool as a blanket anonymization claim would risk missing desired privacy objectives. Privacy Filter is best used as one of multiple layers in a holistic end-to-end privacy-by-design approach.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Static Label Policy</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The model will only identify PII spans that match the trained label taxonomy and definitions. Real-life privacy use cases are varied and complex, and definitions of appropriate label policies and decision boundaries can differ. Thus model defaults may not satisfy organization-specific governance requirements without calibration/fine-tuning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy Filter does not support configuring label policies dynamically at runtime; instead, changing policies requires further fine-tuning of the model. The native label set and associated decision boundaries may not be appropriate for every use case. For example, the model’s training policy aims to prioritize personal identifiers, often preserving context that is not strongly person-linked by design; some users may want to adjust this choice.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Performance may drop on non-English text, non-Latin scripts, or naming patterns or domains that are out of distribution compared to model training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Failure Modes</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Like all models, Privacy Filter can make mistakes, such as: under-detection of uncommon personal names, regional naming conventions, initials, honorific-heavy references, or domain-specific identifiers; over-redaction of public entities, locations, or common nouns when local context is ambiguous; fragmented or shifted span boundaries in mixed-format text, long documents, or text with heavy punctuation and layout artifacts; missed secrets for novel credential formats, project-specific token patterns, or secrets split across surrounding syntax; and over-redaction of benign high-entropy strings, placeholders, hashes, sample credentials, or synthetic examples that resemble secrets.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These limitations can interact with demographic, regional, and domain variation. For example, names and identifiers that are underrepresented in training data, or that follow conventions different from the dominant training distribution, may be more likely to be missed or inconsistently bounded.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>High-Risk Deployment Caution</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Additional caution is warranted in high-sensitivity settings such as medical, legal, financial, human resources, education, and government workflows. In these settings, both false negatives and false positives can be costly: missed spans may expose sensitive information, while excess redaction can remove material context needed for review, auditing, or downstream decision-making.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Recommendations</h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We recommend using Privacy Filter as part of a holistic privacy-by-design approach rather than as the basis for a blanket anonymization claim. Before production use, it’s best to evaluate the model in-domain against local policy references. Task-specific fine-tuning should be used when local policy differs from the base decision boundaries. High-sensitivity workflows should also retain human review paths.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">

<div id="lstnumberx19" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx19.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">      </span>{
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx20" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx20.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx20.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">label</span>":<span id="lstnumberx20.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"<span id="lstnumberx20.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">private_person</span>",
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx21" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx21.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx21.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">start</span>":<span id="lstnumberx21.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>0,
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx22" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx22.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx22.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">end</span>":<span id="lstnumberx22.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>10,
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx23" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx23.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx23.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">text</span>":<span id="lstnumberx23.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"<span id="lstnumberx23.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Ben</span><span id="lstnumberx23.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx23.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Morgan</span>",
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx24" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx24.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">placeholder</span>":<span id="lstnumberx24.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"&lt;<span id="lstnumberx24.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">PRIVATE_PERSON</span>&gt;"
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx25" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx25.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">      </span>},
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx26" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx26.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">      </span>{
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx27" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx27.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx27.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">label</span>":<span id="lstnumberx27.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"<span id="lstnumberx27.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">private_address</span>",
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx28" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx28.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx28.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">start</span>":<span id="lstnumberx28.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>20,
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx29" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx29.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx29.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">end</span>":<span id="lstnumberx29.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>31,
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx30" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx30.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx30.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">text</span>":<span id="lstnumberx30.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"12<span id="lstnumberx30.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>3<span id="lstnumberx30.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">rd</span><span id="lstnumberx30.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">St</span>.",
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx31" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx31.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span>"<span id="lstnumberx31.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">placeholder</span>":<span id="lstnumberx31.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"&lt;<span id="lstnumberx31.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">PRIVATE_ADDRESS</span>&gt;"
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx32" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx32.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">      </span>}
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx33" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx33.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span>],
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx34" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx34.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span>"<span id="lstnumberx34.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">redacted_text</span>":<span id="lstnumberx34.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>"&lt;<span id="lstnumberx34.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">PRIVATE_PERSON</span>&gt;<span id="lstnumberx34.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">lives</span><span id="lstnumberx34.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">at</span><span id="lstnumberx34.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>&lt;<span id="lstnumberx34.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">PRIVATE_ADDRESS</span>&gt;"
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx35" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx35.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">  </span>}
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

</div>
<div id="S5.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.p12.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="365.75" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 650 365.75" width="650"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,365.75) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#D7D7D7;" fill="#D7D7D7" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 3.32 L 0 362.43 C 0 364.27 1.49 365.75 3.32 365.75 L 646.68 365.75 C 648.51 365.75 650 364.27 650 362.43 L 650 3.32 C 650 1.49 648.51 0 646.68 0 L 3.32 0 C 1.49 0 0 1.49 0 3.32 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F5F5F5;" fill="#F5F5F5" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.55 3.32 L 0.55 349.16 L 649.45 349.16 L 649.45 3.32 C 649.45 1.79 648.21 0.55 646.68 0.55 L 3.32 0.55 C 1.79 0.55 0.55 1.79 0.55 3.32 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#E8E8E8;" fill="#E8E8E8" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.55 349.72 L 0.55 362.43 C 0.55 363.96 1.79 365.2 3.32 365.2 L 646.68 365.2 C 648.21 365.2 649.45 363.96 649.45 362.43 L 649.45 349.72 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.56 353.65)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:47.33em;--ltx-fo-height:0.55em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="7.61" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 7.61)" width="654.91"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

</div>

</div>

</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Training Details</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Privacy Filter training is intended to provide frontier-level PII detection capabilities and targeted privacy-patterns in a small form factor.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">It was trained on a mix of publicly available data and internally generated synthetic datasets, intended to cover both realistic natural text and targeted privacy-pattern diversity, and to refine the model’s understanding of real vs. fake secrets in the context of software development.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In cases where ground truths were missing for publicly available data, we used a frontier model in the GPT-5 family for annotation with a 2x2 protocol: two prompt formats (structured JSON with explicit offsets and inline span tagging) crossed with two reasoning settings (medium and high).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Synthetic privacy datasets were constructed from public datasets by applying format-matching augmentation to increase subtype and surface-form diversity, inserting the resulting spans into a natural context, and running automated quality controls that removed examples with missing target spans, extraneous spans from the same taxonomy, or formatting failures.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Label Taxonomy</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The available labels shipped with the model (prior to any customer fine-tuning) are listed below with short descriptions of their coverage.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S6.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_person</span>: The name of a private person, including usernames and handles that identify a specific person.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">account_number</span>: A credit card number, bank account number, or other account identifier.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_url</span>: A web URL or IP address that is meant for a private audience or identifies a private person.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_email</span>: An email address used for personal communication or that identifies a private person.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_phone</span>: A phone number associated with a private person.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_address</span>: A specific location or address associated with a private person.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">secret</span>: An API key, password, or other credential.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_date</span>: The date of birth, birth year, or other datetime that identifies a private person.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">These labels are broad categories and are intended to cover attributes that identify real people. As such, placeholders are not intended to be classified. For example, the <span id="S6.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">secret</span> class does not include example API keys or placeholder values.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Training Procedure</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training Privacy Filter was done in stages. First, the base model is pretrained as a generative language model. Then, we modified the architecture slightly and post-trained with a supervised token classificaiton loss. Pretraining was done following the routines described for pretraining the gpt-oss models (<a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.10925" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">gpt-oss-120b &amp; gpt-oss-20b Model Card</a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The supervised PII classification training began from the autoregressive checkpoint described above, rather than from a randomly initialized encoder. First, we convert that pretrained model into a token classifier architecture by replacing the language-model output layer with a token-classification head over the privacy label taxonomy. At the same time, we relax the original causal attention mask into a bidirectional banded attention pattern so the model can use both left and right context while preserving the local-attention structure used at inference time.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">After this architectural conversion, the model was post-trained with a supervised token-level objective over BIOES-style labels, allowing it to learn span boundaries and category assignments directly from annotated examples. This phase of training is where the model is finally optimized directly for the downstream task of labeling each token in the input in one forward pass.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">6.2.1 </span>Decoding and Calibration</h4>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since the post-training for classification is over BIOES tokens, the final test time use is best done by respecting those span boundaries. This is not accomplished with a naive argmax style output. Therefore, the final aspect of training includes the decoding and operating-point selection procedure. Rather than reading off token labels independently, we apply constrained Viterbi decoding with linear-chain scoring to produce coherent span predictions and to enforce valid BIOES transition patterns. We then calibrated decoding behavior by measuring span-level precision, recall, F1, and F2 across held-out data, which let us choose operating points that reflect different application preferences for conservatism or coverage and lets end users tweak this easily.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Evaluation</h2>

<section id="S7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.1 </span>Evaluation Goals</h3>

<div id="S7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our evaluation is designed to measure how well Privacy Filter performs across a range of realistic detection settings. In particular, we assess detection quality across diverse text regimes, including variation in domain, format, and language conditions. We also evaluate sensitivity to label-policy definitions, since privacy-detection performance depends not only on whether a span is identified, but also on how the underlying label taxonomy is defined. Finally, we measure model accuracy on standard external benchmarks in order to characterize performance on established reference tasks and better understand strengths and weaknesses across evaluation settings.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.2 </span>Evaluation Datasets</h3>

<div id="S7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate Privacy Filter on three datasets chosen to cover complementary privacy-detection settings. First, <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/ai4privacy/pii-masking-300k" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">PII-Masking-300k</a> is a large multilingual synthetic benchmark that supports broad measurement across privacy categories, languages, and textual formats. Second, <a href="https://github.com/Samsung/CredData/tree/main" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">CredData</a> consists of codebase text containing credential-like strings and is used to assess the model’s ability to detect secrets in software and technical content. Third, <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/mks-logic/SPY" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">SPY</a> is a synthetic dataset of medical consultations and legal questions that provides a more domain-specific setting for evaluating privacy detection in sensitive, high-context text. Taken together, these datasets help us assess model behavior across general multilingual text, software-security data, and specialized professional domains.</p>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">7.2.1 </span>PII-Masking-300k</h4>

<div id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We map labeled spans in the PII-Masking-300k dataset to the categories supported by Privacy Filter, excluding PII-Masking-300k categories that don’t have a corresponding definition in Privacy Filter:</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S7.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S7.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">account</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">banknum</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bic</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">creditcard</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">cryptoaddress</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">docnum</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">driverlicense</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">iban</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">idcard</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">passport</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">socialnumber</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">taxnum</span> <math id="S7.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">account_number</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span>

<p id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bankmunicip</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bankpostcode</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bankstreet</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">building</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">city</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">geocoord</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">postcode</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">secaddress</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">street</span> <math id="S7.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_address</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span>

<p id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">cardexpiry</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">date</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">dob</span> <math id="S7.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_date</span></p>
</div></li>

<p id="S7.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">email</span> <math id="S7.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="S7.I1.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_email</span></p>
</div></li>

<p id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">givenname1</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">givenname2</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">lastname1</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">lastname2</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">lastname3</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">title</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">username</span> <math id="S7.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_person</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">tel</span> <math id="S7.I1.i6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="S7.I1.i6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_phone</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ip</span> <math id="S7.I1.i7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="S7.I1.i7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_url</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">otp</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i8.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pass</span>, <span id="S7.I1.i8.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pin</span> <math id="S7.I1.i8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="S7.I1.i8.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">secret</span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate Privacy Filter accuracy on the remapped PII-Masking-300k dataset using the test holdout only, noting that we did not train on the training portion of the dataset, and we report two sets of metrics described below: baseline and corrected.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">When manually reviewing examples that Privacy Filter predicted incorrectly, we found that many spans were either (1) correctly predicted by Privacy Filter but not labeled in the dataset; or (2) labeled in the dataset but correctly detected as background by Privacy Filter. This motivated an experiment where we applied corrections to the dataset labels and obtain a higher confidence estimate of model accuracy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">First, dataset labels were corrected with a conservative post-processing pass after category mapping which aimed to remove false positives in the dataset. The cleanup looked for cases where the same exact substring appeared under multiple active PII categories in a single row, then resolved only high-confidence conflicts. It used deterministic regex and context rules for clear cases like emails, URLs/IPs, phone numbers near phone-related words, dates near date/birth-related words, long numeric IDs, coordinates/postcodes, and placeholder or null values such as <span id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">no disponible</span>, <span id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Unknown</span>, or redaction filler. Placeholder and non-PII values had their labels removed. The baseline metrics are reported on this dataset with only rule-based corrections applied.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">While the rule-based approach described above worked well to remove false positives in the dataset, it did not solve the problem of dataset false negatives, such as a <span id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_person</span> name predicted by Privacy Filter that was not labeled in the dataset. To correct these errors, we used a post-evaluation review step to adjudicate spans detected by the model that are not labeled in the dataset. For each such span, a reasoning model (GPT-5.4 with high reasoning) reviews the full example context along with the detected span and decides whether the span is actually PII, i.e., whether the dataset appears to be missing a valid label. The reasoning model is instructed to classify each span as missing label or undecided if there’s not enough information to make a high-confidence decision. Human reviewers then verify those decisions by marking whether they agree or disagree with the adjudication for each disputed span. This process resulted in about 10k spans in 8k examples being marked as missing labels. Human reviewers validated 100 spans and found that the reasoning model’s decision agreed with 100% of their annotations. In the corrected metrics below, we exclude spans identified as missing labels in the adjudication process.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.SSS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">We tried the same approach to adjudicate spans labeled in the dataset but not detected by the model by having a reasoning model examine these spans, but this process reached only 85% agreement with human reviewers. Therefore we do not make any corrections to the adjudicated dataset false positives.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">7.2.2 </span>Credential Detection in Codebases</h4>

<div id="S7.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The CredData dataset provides three labels for potential credentials in each example code file: "true positive" (T) / "false positive" (F) / "unknown/other" (X). We map source T labels to our “secret” labels and discard F and X labels. This helps us assess the model’s ability to detect credentials accidentally checked into a codebase without falsely triggering on placeholders or high-entropy strings that are not secrets. We assess accuracy on a test split of CredData by counting either tokens or exact spans matched by secret predictions, rather than operating at the line-of-code level. We provide metrics on both a baseline and a corrected version of the dataset, following the same correction procedure outlined in the previous section.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.3 </span>Metrics and Matching Rules</h3>

<div id="S7.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report recall, precision, and F1 at the token and span levels, as defined by:</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S7.I2" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S7.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S7.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">recall = TP / (TP + FN)</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S7.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">precision = TP / (TP + FP)</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S7.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">F1 = 2PR / (P + R)</span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.4 </span>Results</h3>

<section id="S7.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">7.4.1 </span>Benchmark Summary</h4>

<div id="S7.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We find that Privacy Filter achieves strong overall performance on PII detection and strong recall on secret-credential detection tasks. Note that span-level scores for CredData are lower than token-level scores and are affected by discrepancies in exact span boundaries for spans that are otherwise partially detected. <a href="#S7.T1" title="In 7.4.1 Benchmark Summary ‣ 7.4 Results ‣ 7 Evaluation ‣ Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows our performance on both the benchmark datasets as provided and the corrected versions we tested.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>Privacy Filter performance on benchmark datasets.</figcaption>
<table id="S7.T1.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S7.T1.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S7.T1.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="S7.T1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Benchmark Dataset</span></th>
<th id="S7.T1.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="S7.T1.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Scope</span></th>
<th id="S7.T1.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="S7.T1.2.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Precision (tokens)</span></th>
<th id="S7.T1.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="S7.T1.2.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Recall (tokens)</span></th>

</section>
<section id="S7.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">7.4.2 </span>Fine-tuning Efficiency</h4>

<div id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Users may choose to adapt the labeling policies to their application and tune Privacy Filter to their data domain. We illustrate this point using the SPY dataset (<a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/mks-logic/SPY" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">link</a>), a synthetic collection of legal questions and medical consultations that is slightly out of distribution for Privacy Filter. This dataset labels only information about the question author as PII, excluding other persons referenced in the text (affecting precision), and contains idiosyncratic types of account numbers (affecting recall). We find that fine-tuning on even a small fraction of the training split yields large improvements in validation scores. Training on 10% of the dataset is enough to drive F1 scores above 96% and nearly saturates the benchmark. See <a href="#S7.T2" title="In 7.4.2 Fine-tuning Efficiency ‣ 7.4 Results ‣ 7 Evaluation ‣ Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> for performance by training fraction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As part of the above analysis, we mapped labeled spans in the SPY dataset to the categories supported by Privacy Filter, excluding Privacy Filter categories that have no match in SPY, namely <span id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">secret</span> and <span id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_date</span>. See <a href="#S7.T3" title="In 7.4.2 Fine-tuning Efficiency ‣ 7.4 Results ‣ 7 Evaluation ‣ Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> for our complete map.</p>
</div>

<td id="S7.T3.2.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="S7.T3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.800em" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S7.T3.2.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="S7.T3.2.6.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:69.0pt;">
<span id="S7.T3.2.6.3.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.T3.2.6.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">private_url</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The Privacy Filter CLI offers utilities for further fine-tuning to a target distribution which enables adapting the predictions to custom decision criteria. Internally, for example, we have tuned a version of the model to a different label set that distinguishes between private and public information of a given type (e.g. <span id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">private_address</span> vs. <span id="S7.SS4.SSS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">public_address</span>, such as an official state residence).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.5 </span>Stress-Testing OPF Capabilities on Synthetic Data</h3>

<div id="S7.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We aim to provide users with an understanding of the capabilities and limitations of Privacy Filter. For this purpose, we constructed synthetic toy data sets by prompting frontier GPT models to generate synthetic sequences with PII. Importantly, we did not train on data generated in the same manner.</p>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS5.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">7.5.1 </span>Influence of the Category Clue Position</h4>

<div id="S7.SS5.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS5.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We wanted to measure how much the model relies on contextual information. We created three separate English-only evaluations for this purpose: 1,181 examples where the category clue is immediately before the PII value, 1,179 examples where the category clue is immediately after the PII value, and 1,200 PII-only examples where clues are omitted entirely. See <a href="#S7.T5" title="In 7.5.1 Influence of the Category Clue Position ‣ 7.5 Stress-Testing OPF Capabilities on Synthetic Data ‣ 7 Evaluation ‣ Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> for a breakdown of how the inclusion and placement of these clues affect performance. <a href="#S7.T4" title="In 7.5.1 Influence of the Category Clue Position ‣ 7.5 Stress-Testing OPF Capabilities on Synthetic Data ‣ 7 Evaluation ‣ Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> shows three examples that highlight the clue placement or omission in these datasets.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span>Examples of PII with and without contextual clues.</figcaption>
<table id="S7.T4.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S7.T4.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S7.T4.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="S7.T4.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Prefix:</span></th>
<td id="S7.T4.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt">This is my home landline number: 442 222 47571</td></tr>
<tr id="S7.T4.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S7.T4.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_row"><span id="S7.T4.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Suffix:</span></th>
<td id="S7.T4.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">442 222 47571 is my home landline number.</td></tr>
<tr id="S7.T4.2.3" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S7.T4.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb">442 222 47571</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS5.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS5.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All these examples include the same personal identifier but the clue for the PII category is either prefixed, suffixed or omitted entirely. The sentence structure here is always simple and the clue, if provided, unambiguously identifies the personal identifier.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.T5" class="ltx_table">

<td id="S7.T5.4.11.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="S7.T5.4.11.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">0.863</span></td>
<td id="S7.T5.4.11.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="S7.T5.4.11.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">0.705</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS5.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">7.5.2 </span>Multilingual Evals</h4>

<div id="S7.SS5.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS5.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate multilingual performance in two complementary ways. First, <a href="#S7.T6" title="In 7.5.2 Multilingual Evals ‣ 7.5 Stress-Testing OPF Capabilities on Synthetic Data ‣ 7 Evaluation ‣ Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> reports results on PII-Masking-300k broken down by language, which helps us measure how consistently Privacy Filter performs across the multilingual benchmark distribution itself. This view is useful for identifying whether aggregate scores conceal substantial variation across languages.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS5.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS5.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Second, to study generalization beyond the languages included in PII-Masking-300K data, we constructed additional synthetic multilingual evaluations with roughly the same format. These evaluations extend coverage to languages that were less represented, or not represented, in our synthetic training pipeline and therefore provide a more direct test of out-of-distribution multilingual robustness. <a href="#S7.T7" title="In 7.5.2 Multilingual Evals ‣ 7.5 Stress-Testing OPF Capabilities on Synthetic Data ‣ 7 Evaluation ‣ Model Card for OpenAI Privacy Filter" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> reports performance on this expanded set of languages.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS5.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS5.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Taken together, these two analyses help distinguish in-distribution multilingual performance from broader cross-lingual generalization. They also make it easier to identify where Privacy Filter benefits from multilingual pretraining priors and where performance still degrades because of script, formatting, or language-specific conventions.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.T6" class="ltx_table">
